items.prompt: Why does the worked minimum-window function reject negative values?

options.text: The function requires sorted input so that either pointer can move arbitrarily
options.why: This window needs nonnegative values, not sortedness; its specific add-and-shrink proof does not permit arbitrary pointer movement.

options.text: Negative values make all thresholds impossible
options.why: Some negative-containing lists have qualifying windows.

options.text: The rejection is only cosmetic and unrelated to correctness
options.why: The proof depends directly on monotonic sum changes.

options.text: Removing a negative can increase the sum and break the shrink logic
options.why: The stated nonnegative proof no longer applies.

items.explanation: A pattern must carry its preconditions. The counterexample shows a valid shorter window can be missed without nonnegativity.
